sections.theory:
Chapter 3 — Bank

Concept of a bank

A bank means such an institution which takes the surplus money of common people (saved from expenditure) and keeps it with itself as a trust for safekeeping, and on demand for its return pays it to them. Further, the bank gives the money lying with it as loans to needy traders, landlords and industrialists and earns interest and mark-up.

Professor Crowther:

“A bank does the business of its own and others’ debts. The bank takes loans from common people and gives loans to the needy, and in this way creates credit money (Credit Money).”

Professor Stanley Fischer:

“The commercial banks of the present age are profit-earning financial intermediaries. On the one side they obtain financial sums through deposits or borrowing (Borrowing), and on the other side they use these same sums for giving loans onwards.”

Kinds of banks

There are many kinds of banks; every bank performs its own particular functions, whose detail is given below.

1. Central Bank

This is a government bank and is responsible for making the financial and currency system of the country stable. The central bank of Pakistan is the State Bank of Pakistan. The important functions of the central bank are as follows.

i. It issues currency notes.

ii. It performs banking services for the government.

iii. It keeps the reserve capital of commercial banks in its custody.

iv. It makes the money market of the country organised and stable.

2. Commercial Bank

These are generally established with the joint capital of people and perform the functions of banking, e.g.

i. They receive deposits.

ii. They give loans to business people.

iii. They transfer money.

iv. They provide finance for foreign trade.

v. They lend capital for a short period.

Chapter 3 — Bank

Concept of a bank

A bank means such an institution which takes the surplus money of common people (saved from expenditure) and keeps it with itself as a trust for safekeeping, and on demand for its return pays it to them. Further, the bank gives the money lying with it as loans to needy traders, landlords and industrialists and earns interest and mark-up.

Professor Crowther:

“A bank does the business of its own and others’ debts. The bank takes loans from common people and gives loans to the needy, and in this way creates credit money (Credit Money).”

Professor Stanley Fischer:

“The commercial banks of the present age are profit-earning financial intermediaries. On the one side they obtain financial sums through deposits or borrowing (Borrowing), and on the other side they use these same sums for giving loans onwards.”

Kinds of banks

There are many kinds of banks; every bank performs its own particular functions, whose detail is given below.

1. Central Bank

This is a government bank and is responsible for making the financial and currency system of the country stable. The central bank of Pakistan is the State Bank of Pakistan. The important functions of the central bank are as follows.

i. It issues currency notes.

ii. It performs banking services for the government.

iii. It keeps the reserve capital of commercial banks in its custody.

iv. It makes the money market of the country organised and stable.

2. Commercial Bank

These are generally established with the joint capital of people and perform the functions of banking, e.g.

i. They receive deposits.

ii. They give loans to business people.

iii. They transfer money.

iv. They provide finance for foreign trade.

v. They lend capital for a short period.

بنک سے مراد ایسا ادارہ ہے جو عام لوگوں سے ان کی فاضل رقم (خرچ سے بچی ہوئی) لے کر اپنے پاس حفاظت کے لیے بطور امانت رکھتا ہے۔ اور واپس مانگنے پر انہیں ادا کر دیتا ہے۔ نیز بنک اپنے پاس پڑی ہوئی رقم ضرورت مند تاجروں، زمینداروں اور صنعتکاروں کو قرضہ دے کر سود اور مارک اپ کماتا ہے۔

”موجودہ دور کے کمرشل بنک منافع کمانے والے مالی متوسلین ہوتے ہیں۔ وہ ایک طرف امانتوں یا قرض گیری (Borrowing) کے ذریعے مالی رقوم حاصل کرتے ہیں۔ اور دوسری طرف یہی رقوم آگے قرضہ دینے کیلئے استعمال کرتے ہیں۔“

بینکوں کی اقسام

بینکوں کی کئی قسمیں ہیں ہر بنک اپنے مخصوص فرائض سرانجام دیتا ہے جس کی تفصیل ذیل میں ہے۔

1۔ مرکزی بینک: (Central Bank)

یہ سرکاری بینک ہوتا ہے اور ملک کے مالی اور کرنسی نظام کو مستحکم بنانے کا ذمہ دار ہوتا ہے پاکستان کا مرکزی بینک سٹیٹ بینک آف پاکستان ہے۔ مرکزی بینک کے اہم فرائض درج ذیل ہیں۔

ii۔ حکومت کے لیے بنکاری کی خدمات ادا کرتا ہے۔

iii۔ کمرشل بینکوں کا محفوظ سرمایہ اپنی تحویل میں رکھتا ہے۔

iv۔ ملک کے بازارِ زر کو منظم اور مستحکم بناتا ہے۔

3. Industrial Bank

These banks give loans to industries for a long period and play an important role in the industrial progress of the country. In Pakistan the work of giving loans to industries is being done by the “Pakistan Industrial Development Bank” (i.e. Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan, IDBP).

4. Agricultural Bank

These give loans to cultivators for the progress and promotion of agriculture. In Pakistan, to provide loans to agriculture, the “Pakistan Agricultural Development Bank” has been established. Besides this, cooperative banks too give loans to cultivators.

5. Exchange banks (Exchangs Bank)

These do the business of foreign money, provide finance to foreign trade, and issue drafts for payments in foreign countries.

6. Saving Bank

Their purpose is that people be encouraged to save. Thus these take small savings from the public and give interest or profit on them. (In Islam interest is forbidden; therefore the government is taking steps to end interest at the level of Pakistan.) Banks of this kind exist in post offices; they are called Post Office Saving Banks.

7. Public Sector Bank

These banks are owned by the government, and the government also controls these banks, e.g. National Bank and Habib Bank etc.

8. Private Sector Bank

These banks are established through mutual cooperation, for example Muslim Commercial Bank and Allied Bank etc.

9. Cooperative Banks

Generally these banks are established for giving short- and medium-term loans for rural development. In Pakistan these banks are established under the Cooperative Act 1925.

10. Domestic Banks

These banks are registered within the country and perform their functions within the border of that same country.

11. Foreign Banks

These are such banks as are doing work in one country, but their head office and ownership are in another country.
